$comment: Single source of the workspace test-coverage floor (CLAUDE.md Rule 14). Every project's `vitest.config.*` reads `thresholds` from here instead of restating the four numbers, so the floor is one edit and no project can sit below it while looking compliant. Consumers: every vitest config in the workspace; shared/tools/dev-cli/src/run-node-tests.mjs, which turns the same numbers into CLI flags for the one project on Node's built-in test runner, since an nx:run-commands string cannot read JSON; shared/tools/dev-cli/src/run-go-tests.mjs, which holds every Go project's `go test` run to the `statements` floor — the one metric Go coverage measures; and shared/tools/dev-cli/src/check-project-conventions.mjs, which requires a project that has tests to reach this file through one of those two roads rather than declare its own numbers. `statements` has no consumer on the Node runner — it exposes no such threshold — so that project is held to three of these four, loudly: run-node-tests refuses to run if `statements` is ever raised above `lines`. The value lives at the repo root rather than inside one project because a cross-project source import would be an edge the Nx project graph cannot see — the same reason journey-markers.config.json, languages.config.json and practice-index.json sit here. nx.json's `coverageConfig` named input puts this file in every test target's cache key, so a change to the floor re-runs the suites it governs instead of replaying a cached green — but a project that declares its own target `inputs` REPLACES those defaults, so it must restate `coverageConfig` there (eslint-local-rules does).
